purpose: Polatuzumab vedotin is used to treat a type of blood cancer called diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). It is typically used when the cancer has come back or has not responded to other treatments. It is often given together with other cancer medicines to help fight the disease more effectively.
how_it_works: Think of this medicine as a smart missile. It has two parts: an antibody that acts like a GPS, finding and locking onto cancer cells, and a powerful chemotherapy drug attached to it. Once it finds the cancer cell, it delivers the chemotherapy directly inside the cell to destroy it, while leaving healthy cells more protected than traditional chemotherapy would.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired, nausea, diarrhea, low blood cell counts (which can increase risk of infection, bleeding, or anemia), numbness or tingling in hands and feet (nerve damage), decreased appetite, and fever.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious nerve damage (peripheral neuropathy) — tell your doctor right away if you feel numbness, tingling, or weakness. It can severely lower your blood cell counts, raising your risk of serious infections or bleeding. Rare but serious brain infections (PML) have been reported. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during and after treatment. Liver problems can also occur and your doctor will monitor your blood regularly.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) at a clinic or hospital, usually once every 21 days (one cycle). The dose is based on your body weight. Your doctor will decide how many cycles you need, typically around 6 cycles. Each infusion session may take about 90 minutes or longer depending on how you tolerate it.
